Vaccine

/vak-SEEN/ — rhymes with keen · noun

Hear It

What It Means

A vaccine is a substance given to the body, usually by injection, that trains the immune system to protect against a specific disease.

The new vaccine protects against three strains of the flu.

Worked Example

Before traveling to Africa, travelers lined up at the clinic to receive injections that would prepare their immune systems against malaria.

Vaccine is precise because it specifically names a preventive injection that trains the immune system to fight a disease, not just any medical injection or general health measure.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

inoculation: introducing a germ to build protection

immunization: process of making someone immune to disease

serum: fluid injected to fight or prevent illness

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

virus: the germ a vaccine defends against

Where it sits · how strong the defense against illness — susceptibility → precaution → immunity → vaccine

susceptibility vs. vaccine: Susceptibility sits at the opposite end from a vaccine; susceptibility means being open to disease, while a vaccine trains the body to fight it off.

precaution vs. vaccine: A precaution is a milder safeguard than a vaccine; a precaution is any general care taken, while a vaccine actively builds specific protection into the immune system.

immunity vs. vaccine: Immunity is the full result a vaccine aims for; a vaccine is the substance given, while immunity is the finished protection it produces.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — vacc-

Root — vacc-: cow (Latin)

Suffix — -ine

Suffix — -ine: pertaining to; of the nature of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Vacc- means 'cow' and -ine means 'pertaining to,' so vaccine literally means 'of the cow' — a reminder that the first vaccine used cowpox to protect against smallpox.

Use the root in a new word: vaccinate

Use the root in a new word: vaccinate: When a nurse vaccinates you, she gives you a vaccine; both trace back to the Latin word for 'cow,' since the first vaccine came from cowpox.

Word Building

Word Choice

neutral / formal

Vaccine is the standard, precise term for a preventive injection that trains the immune system. Use it when discussing specific medical prevention. For the broader concept of building immunity or general protective measures, simpler words like 'precaution' or 'immunization' may be clearer.
